subject: Scam of the week: the $6.99 "unpaid toll" text
preheader: Toll agencies bill through your account or by mail. Don't tap the link.
html:
Toll agencies bill through your account or by mail. Don't tap the link.
Scam Decoded · Scam of the week · 2027-01-14

Toll texts come back every January, and this week they're everywhere. Here's the one to delete, plus two that are still going around after the holidays.

Urgent scam alert

"Unpaid toll" texts are back

Arrives by: text · From: a toll agency, from a number or email address you don't know (fictional example)

NOTICE: You have an outstanding toll balance of $6.99. To avoid a $50 late fee and license suspension, pay by 11:59 PM today: ezdrive-tollpay.top

3 tells

  1. A small amount with a big threat attached: late fees, license suspension, today.
  2. A link that isn't your toll agency's real website, often with an odd ending like .top or .xyz.
  3. It arrives as a text from a number you don't know, sometimes even if you haven't driven a toll road.

Do this

  1. Don't tap. Log in to your toll account by typing the agency's website yourself, or call the number on your statement.
  2. Check the real balance there. No balance? It's fake.
  3. Forward the text to 7726 (SPAM), and report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Already clicked, paid or shared? Paid on that page? Call your card company today, ask for a new card, and dispute the charge.

Source: FTC: Got a text about unpaid tolls? It's probably a scam

How it works: Unpaid toll texts

Paste a message into our free scam checker

Also going around

  • Fake "fraud team" calls after a data breach (call). It arrives right after breach news, and uses that news to sound believable. The 3 tells
  • "Your package is on hold" texts are spiking before Black Friday (text). A text you didn't sign up for, from a regular phone number, about a package you can't name. The 3 tells

Could you spot it?

Text from First Harbor Bank (fictional)

Your First Harbor sign-in code is 482913. We will never call, text or email to ask for this code. (You just tried to sign in.)

Scam or legit? Take the 12-question quiz for the answer.

Know someone who'd get a message like this? Forward them this email. They can sign up at https://scamdecoded.netlify.app/alerts/.

Educational content, not legal or financial advice. Example messages, names and numbers are fictional. Check current rules with the official source before acting.
